name: Container freight
summary: Drewry container index fell 2% to $4,305 per 40ft on 12 Nov, still above the $4,000 Alert line; next update 19 Nov
state: Drewry's World Container Index fell 2% to $4,305 per 40ft container on 12 Nov and stays above the $4,000 Alert line (Drewry). Shanghai–New York fell 3% to $9,020, its lowest since August, and Shanghai–Rotterdam 3% to $3,504. Drewry expects transpacific rates to fall further but Asia–Europe rates to rise slightly on blank sailings and surcharges from late November; the next index is due on 19 Nov.
for_you: High container rates tend to feed through to retail prices and delivery times for imported goods. Importers on spot contracts are most exposed.
basis_detail: Drewry World Container Index / Freightos Baltic Index
basis_by: Drewry World Container Index / Freightos Baltic Index

sources.title: Drewry WCI Down 2% to $4,305: Transpacific & Asia-Europe Rates Fall

why: Container rates feed through to goods prices months later; spikes are an early inflation and supply-chain warning.
drivers: Chokepoint diversions, capacity, demand, port congestion, tariffs front-running.

rubric.normal: Drewry World Container Index < $2,500/FEU and 1-month change < +30%.
